title: Target-optimized transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) for obsessive-compulsive disorder: neurochemical and neurocognitive mechanisms
summary:
Obsessive-compulsive disorder involves recurring unwanted thoughts and/or repetitive behaviours that can cause considerable burden. Transcranial direct current stimulation, or tDCS, applies a very weak electrical current through electrodes placed on the scalp. No surgery is required.

The aim of this study is to determine which of three stimulation arrangements produces the clearest changes in brain activity, naturally occurring brain chemicals and attention. The study investigates how the stimulation works and is not a therapeutic treatment trial. Improvement in obsessive-compulsive symptoms is not expected from the individual sessions.

People aged 11 to 30 years with a clinically established diagnosis of obsessive-compulsive disorder may participate. Each participant takes part in one of two experiments. Experiment 1 examines the effects of stimulation using MRI and magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Experiment 2 uses EEG and a computer-based attention task.

All participants receive three active stimulation conditions and one sham stimulation condition in a random order. Participation involves one introductory and screening visit followed by four experimental sessions, each separated by at least one week.

interventions.name: Arm 1: Inhibitory pre-SMA tDCS: Cathodal transcranial direct current stimulation over the pre-supplementary motor area (pre-SMA/FCz), with the return electrode over the right mastoid. Stimulation is delivered at 2 mA for 20 minutes.

Arm 2: Excitatory left DLPFC tDCS: Anodal transcranial direct current stimulation over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC/F3), with the return electrode over the right mastoid. Stimulation is delivered at 2 mA for 20 minutes.

Arm 3: Dual-site tDCS: Anodal transcranial direct current stimulation over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC/F3) combined with cathodal stimulation over the pre-supplementary motor area (pre-SMA/FCz). Stimulation is delivered at 2 mA for 20 minutes.

Arm 4: Sham tDCS: Sham transcranial direct current stimulation using the electrode configuration of the dual-site condition. A short ramp-in/ramp-out stimulation is delivered to reproduce the initial sensations of active stimulation without continuous active stimulation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Clinically established diagnosis of obsessive-compulsive disorder according to DSM-5, confirmed by a structured clinical interview (K-SADS-PL for participants under 18 years; SCID-5 for participants aged 18 years or older)
- Intelligence quotient above 85, based on a previously available assessment documented in the medical record
- Ability to participate in the planned procedures, including tDCS and, depending on the experiment, MRI/MRS or EEG and a computer-based task
- Willingness and availability to attend all five scheduled visits
- If psychotropic medication is taken: stable dosage for at least four weeks before enrolment
- Written informed consent from adult participants
- For minors: written informed consent from the legal guardians and written assent from the minor participant
Exclusion criteria:
- Intelligence quotient below 85
- Premature birth before completion of the 37th week of gestation
- Birth weight below 2500 g
- Developmental or neurological disorder, particularly epilepsy or a history of epileptic seizures
- Family history of epileptic seizures
- History of traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness, skull fracture or brain tissue injury
- Bipolar disorder or schizophrenia
- Current suicidality
- Substance abuse
- Serious medical condition, particularly a relevant disease of internal organs or a metabolic disorder
- Acute skin disease or skin lesion at the intended electrode positions
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Cardiac pacemaker, implanted defibrillator, neurostimulator, deep brain stimulation or another active implant
- Metal implant or metallic foreign body incompatible with safe MRI examination
- Claustrophobia or inability to tolerate the MRI examination
- Any other contraindication to tDCS or MRI
- Other relevant psychiatric or neurological comorbidity that could interfere with interpretation of the mechanistic outcomes
- Participation in another interventional study within the previous 30 days
